messages:
sara: Customer reports 401s on Dedicated Private after flipping to their L7 proxy (F5) in front of our VPC gateway. They say SSO cookie appears to be rewritten by the proxy and our gateway isn't turning it into an Authorization header anymore. Repro steps + logs below.

sara: Reproduced locally with their flow:
1) User logs in -> receives `SSO_SESSION` cookie from IdP
2) F5 rewrites cookie path and adds `Set-Cookie: SSO_SESSION=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None`
3) F5 also does a transform to inject `X-Auth-Source: f5` and strips `Authorization`
4) Our dedicated gateway should map cookie -> bearer header via the ext-authz plugin, but returns 401 when request goes through F5.

sara: Sample curl (works if I pass header directly):
```
# works
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private.example.internal/api/v1/predict
# fails when using cookie and proxy in front
curl -i --cookie "SSO_SESSION=<session>" https://private.example.internal/api/v1/predict
```

sara: From gateway debug logs (redacted):
```
[authz] incoming: Cookie: SSO_SESSION=<session>
[authz] transform: -> expected Authorization: Bearer <token>
[ext-authz] upstream returned 401 (no auth header found)
```

logan: A few quick checks: does the F5 preserve `Cookie:` header or rewrite to `Set-Cookie` only on responses? Also check if it terminates TLS and re-issues cookies - that can change path/host and make our cookie matcher not see it.

anya: If the proxy strips `Authorization`, we rely on ext-authz to accept cookie and mint header. Confirm ext-authz config on the dedicated gateway: do we have `cookie_names: ["SSO_SESSION"]` and `cookie_to_header: true`? We had a variant where cookie parsing required `SameSite` absent.

sara: Verified ext-authz config on the tenant: `cookie_map: { SSO_SESSION: authorization }` is present. But customer says cookie name sometimes comes in as `SSO-SESSION` after F5 rewrite (dash vs underscore). Could be normalization mismatch.

logan: That would explain intermittent failures. F5 iRules sometimes normalize names. Our parser treats header/cookie names case-insensitively but underscores/dashes are significant in the cookie name. Quick workaround: add both entries in cookie_map.

sara: I pushed a small test config to their dedicated stack to accept both keys; still seeing 401 for a few requests. Logs show the gateway sees `Cookie: SSO-SESSION=<session>` but `authn` sidecar immediately rejects because `session_lookup` failed against our session store (redis TTL mismatch).

ops-oncall: Two possible paths:
- Fix on F5 to keep cookie name identical (preferred)
- Make our gateway more permissive: include canonicalization rules for `-`/`_` and fall back to token exchange endpoint

anya: Also check sticky session affinity on the L7. If F5 is rebalancing requests across different backend pods, the KV cache for our session-to-token mapping might not be present (we don't persist kcache between pods). Add session affinity or centralize session store.

sara: Repro steps I gave to customer to get us pcap and headers: 1) repeat curl with `-v` capturing full request/response headers 2) run `openssl s_client -connect private.example.internal:443 -msg` if they can 3) capture gateway debug logs with `REDWOOD_GATEWAY_LOG=ext-authz:debug` and share last 200 lines.

logan: Commands for their infra team (share only if they can run inside the VPC):
```
# dump envoy route+listener
istioctl proxy-config listeners <pod> -n redwood-system
istioctl proxy-config routes <pod> -n redwood-system
# check cookie seen by envoy
kubectl logs <gateway-pod> -c gateway --tail=200 | grep Cookie
```

anonbot: infra-bot noted: "ticket #INC-4629 created for dedicated-tenant-503 auth gap; assigned to eng-infra; priority P2"

ops-oncall: Short-term mitigation we can offer customer: a policy to accept `SSO-SESSION` and `SSO_SESSION` and a temporary fallback that allows cookie->jwt exchange via `/internal/auth/exchange` endpoint. We'll coordinate change window.

anya: I'll prepare the config diff and a canary rollout plan: add permissive cookie mapping + enable session affinity for 10% of traffic. If stable, roll to 100%.

sara: Customer asked if this could be related to NLB vs ALB. Note: NLB preserves original TCP, ALB and F5 can rewrite headers. Ask customer which LB they are using in front of F5. Also asked them to confirm whether the F5 is doing TLS offload.

logan: Follow-up: request packet capture between F5 and our VPC ingress (tcpdump) if customer can and redact PII. If we see `Authorization` removed before we get request -> the change needs to be on their proxy.

sara: I'll send the suggested commands and our temporary config. Also asked them for examples of failing `Set-Cookie` headers. Will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:
